opportunities.title: Solar and Battery Resilience Hubs at County Schools
opportunities.summary: Install islandable rooftop solar panels and battery storage systems at elementary schools to serve as neighborhood emergency shelters during grid outages.
opportunities.rationale: The county faces very high natural hazard risk, 13 disaster declarations, and intense summer heat reaching 46.0 C on pavement.
plan: Inspect school structural and electrical infrastructure for solar and battery readiness.
Execute facility use agreements with local school district officials.
Procure engineering contractors for solar array and battery storage installation.
Install switchgear, rooftop solar arrays, and islanding battery storage systems.
Establish operational emergency shelter protocols with county disaster coordinators.
Commission and test backup power systems under simulated grid outages.
first_steps: Inspect school structural and electrical infrastructure for solar and battery readiness.
Execute facility use agreements with local school district officials.
Procure engineering contractors for solar array and battery storage installation.
Install switchgear, rooftop solar arrays, and islanding battery storage systems.
Establish operational emergency shelter protocols with county disaster coordinators.
Commission and test backup power systems under simulated grid outages.
compliance: Obtain facility alteration approvals from the Division of the State Architect.
Submit interconnection and net energy metering applications to Los Angeles Department of Water & Power.

need_fits.text: Provides emergency backup power, clean air filtration, and cooling shelter during heat waves, inland flooding, and wildfire emergencies.

course_of_action: Assess Mountain View Elementary School roof load and electrical panels.
Install solar panels and battery storage for emergency power.
Designate community cooling and clean air intake spaces.
compliance: Verify building code compliance with municipal education facility standards.
Complete utility interconnection screening with local electric utility.

course_of_action: Survey Plainview Elementary School for rooftop solar array placement.
Install battery storage system with automatic microgrid transfer switch.
Integrate emergency communication equipment into critical backup load circuits.
compliance: Obtain structural safety sign-off from state school facility regulators.
Submit interconnection paperwork to local municipal electric utility.

opportunities.summary: Deploy grid-scale battery storage and solar arrays at retiring natural gas generating stations utilizing existing high-voltage substation grid connections.
opportunities.rationale: The county has 16 fossil plants with retiring units, severe ozone of 0.101 ppm, and high residential power rates of 32.0 cents per kWh.
plan: Coordinate redevelopment timelines with plant operators and utility grid planners.
Survey vacant plant acreage for battery energy storage system footprints.
Submit interconnection reuse requests for existing 220 kV and 230 kV connections.
Procure EPC contractors utilizing local utility and trades workforce.
Install modular lithium-ion battery storage enclosures and safety systems.
Commission clean capacity into local balancing authority grid dispatch.

Survey vacant plant acreage for battery energy storage system footprints.

Deploys lower-cost utility solar and storage utilizing existing high-voltage transmission interconnects, helping reduce retail electricity rates.

compliance: Check environmental remediation compliance for retired turbine footprint.
Obtain grid connection transfer approval from regional grid operator.

File coastal development and air quality management permits.

narrative.summary: Los Angeles County faces severe natural hazards, widespread water impairment, poor air quality, and large uncaptured landfill gas potential. This program directly tackles these priorities by deploying solar-and-battery resilience hubs at local schools, restoring impaired river corridors, and converting retiring fossil power capacity to clean storage and solar. It also captures energy at candidate landfill gas sites, plants extensive shade trees across public school grounds to counter severe surface heat, and offers community solar subscriptions on reclaimed brownfield acreage to lower electricity bills for renter households.
caveats: The opportunities were written by Gemini from the needs, factors and sites in this report. Each was checked to use only this report's needs, sites and numbers. Feasibility and cost were not checked. Course-of-action and compliance lines are planning checks, not legal advice; confirm permits and local rules with counsel and the right agencies.
Figures marked as estimates are rough. The assumptions behind each one are listed with it.
A listed funding program is a lead to check, not a finding that the county or project is eligible. Confirm status and deadlines with the agency.
EPA's landfill database does not include every landfill.
Electricity bill and grid carbon figures are state averages, not county figures.
